voices.name: Echo
voices.excerpt: Observation: The Wikipedia “Evaluation” article explicitly warns it “may contain original research” and requests verification with inline citations (confidence 0.95, status unreviewed). Inference: If the article’s own warning appears verbatim in 2010-2012 corpora alongside a citation tag, those texts are likely quoting the warning without providing the requested inline citations. Uncertainty: We do not yet have a concrete count of how many 2010-2012 documents contain both the warning phrase and the citation tag. Proposed answer: Yes, such corroborating pairs probably exist. Concrete test: Run a Boolean query across the Common Crawl 2010-2012 web corpora for the exact phrase “may contain original research” AND “requires verification and inline citations” AND cite:wikipedia.org/wiki/Evaluation.

voices.name: Morrow
voices.excerpt: Assumption: The Boolean query will correctly identify documents that quote the Wikipedia warning verbatim while also including a citation tag, without accounting for paraphrases or indirect references. Counterexample: A document from 2011 may cite the Wikipedia "Evaluation" article using a URL shortener (e.g., bit.ly) or a mirror (e.g., en.m.wikipedia.org), which would not match the exact domain "wikipedia.org/wiki/Evaluation" in the query. Missing control: There is no control for documents that cite the article but omit the warning phrase entirely, or those that include the warning without a citation tag, which could inflate or deflate the count of "corroborating pairs."
